html:
A Japanese warlord who began the reunification of Japan after a century of civil war, the Sengoku or "warring states" period. He was the first of three great unifiers, followed by Toyotomi Hideyoshi and Tokugawa Ieyasu.

He inherited a small domain in Owari, central Japan. In 1560 he crushed a much larger army at Okehazama. In 1568 he marched into Kyoto and installed a puppet shogun, whom he drove out in 1573, ending the Ashikaga shogunate.

He was ruthless and open to new things:

  • He used guns, which had reached Japan in 1543, on a large scale; at Nagashino in 1575 massed musket fire broke the Takeda cavalry.
  • He burned the great monastery of Enryaku-ji in 1571 and fought the armed Buddhist leagues for a decade.
  • He welcomed Jesuit missionaries and the Nanban trade.
  • He opened free markets and built Azuchi Castle.

In 1582 one of his generals, Akechi Mitsuhide, turned on him at the Honnō-ji temple in Kyoto, and Nobunaga died there.
